close_reason: Done in 606b98d. Added 'Stream drop and cancellation' section to subscribe_events rustdoc and 'Drop and cancellation' section to WsSession struct rustdoc. Both pin the three contracts (partial buffer discarded, connection released, resumption is caller's job). No behavior change; contracts hold today by Rust ownership + reqwest pool policy.
description:
client.rs:382-549 — pub async fn subscribe_events

The returned BoxStream<'static, Result<SseFrame, ClientError>> has undocumented behavior on caller drop:

1. **Drop mid-frame:** What happens if the caller drops the BoxStream while raw_buf has accumulated 800 KiB of an incomplete frame? The stream's owned state (SseStreamState) is dropped by Rust ownership rules, which drops raw_buf and buf. But the documentation doesn't say so — a caller reading the docs cannot tell whether dropping the stream is safe at any time or whether they need to drain it.

2. **Drop with pending HTTP body:** The underlying resp.bytes_stream() is held inside state.stream. When the caller drops the BoxStream, reqwest's connection should be returned to the pool (or closed). Whether that actually happens cleanly depends on reqwest's internal behavior — undocumented in this crate's API.

3. **Cancel safety:** The unfold loop holds .await across stream.next() and parse_sse_block. If the caller's surrounding code cancels the future (tokio::select!, dropping the join handle), the partial work in raw_buf is lost. The doc-comment doesn't mention cancellation behavior.

For a v0.x crate this is acceptable, but the doc-comment on subscribe_events should add a paragraph: "The returned stream may be dropped at any time. Any partially-accumulated frame data is discarded; the next subscribe_events call will resume from last_event_id if provided." That commits the contract and tells callers what to expect.

Same gap exists for WsSession::next_frame. The struct's drop behavior on a half-received frame is implicit, not explicit.
title: subscribe_events SseStreamState async drop semantics undocumented
